item.title: City of Columbus Convenience Centers Help Residents Reduce, Reuse and Recycle After the Holidays
item.description:
For Immediate Release

December 23, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467; dsbriner@columbus.gov

Contact: Aryeh Alex, 614-338-5004

City of Columbus Convenience Centers Help Residents Tackle Post-Holidays Cleanup

One-Stop Drop-Off Collection of Items like Electronics, String Lights, Cardboard, Furniture and Clothing

When it’s out with the old and in with the new after the holidays, residents can use the City of Columbus Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers as a one-stop solution for environmentally friendly cleanup, reuse and recycling.

Residents may drop off a variety of items at the Convenience Centers, at 2100 Alum Creek Dr. and 1550 Georgesville Rd., for reuse, recycling, composting and proper disposal. After the holidays, households may have more trash, including cardboard and gift wrap, old electronics, bulk items and food scraps that don’t fit, or shouldn’t be disposed of, in their city refuse and recycling containers.

The Convenience Centers accept these items and more, including string lights, donated bicycles and gently used clothing and furniture for reuse. The centers are operated by the city’s Division of Refuse Collection, and staff is available to assist residents with proper sorting when they drop off items.

The city service diverts the amount of trash tonnage taken to the Franklin County Sanitary Landfill to help extend its life and support Columbus Climate Action Plan goals.

The Convenience Centers are open Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. but will be closed on Christmas, Dec. 25, and on New Year’s Day, Jan. 1. Get more information here.

Refuse Collection also offers seven drop-off sites for food scraps composting collection that Columbus residents can access seven days a week, 24 hours a day. The designated outdoor collection containers are located at these city Recreation and Parks sites:

  • Bill McDonald Athletic Complex, 4990 Olentangy River Rd., 43214
  • Dodge Park and Community Center, 667 Sullivant Ave., 43215
  • Scioto Southland Park, 3901 Parsons Ave., 43207
  • Beatty Park and Community Center – 247 N. Ohio Ave., 43203
  • Northeast Park and Howard Community Center – 2505 Cassady Ave., 43219
  • Linden Park and Community Center – 1350 Briarwood Ave., 43211
  • Carriage Place Community Center – 4900 Sawmill Rd., 43235

Get more information about what you can drop off at the food scraps collection sites here.

Columbus Public Service Changes for Christmas and New Year's Day

No Trash, Recycling or Yard Waste Collection Dec. 25 and Jan. 1

For residents assigned a collection color, trash pickup will rotate forward by one day the week of the Christmas holiday:

Thursday, Dec. 26:                        Navy

Friday, Dec. 27:                              Pink

Monday, Dec. 30:                           Ruby

Tuesday, Dec. 31:                          Gold

Note: For Gray collection areas, a collection will be made on Tuesday, Dec. 24, and on Thursday, Jan. 2.

The color-coded collection schedule will rotate forward again on Wednesday, Jan. 1, 2025, for New Year’s Day:

Wednesday, Jan. 1:                       NO COLLECTION

Thursday, Jan. 2:                           Gray

Friday, Jan. 3:                                 Navy

Monday, Jan. 6:                              Pink

Tuesday, Jan. 7:                            Ruby

item.title: City of Columbus To Resurface 99 More Neighborhood Streets
item.description:
For Immediate Release

November 20, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467

dsbriner@columbus.gov

City of Columbus Will Resurface Another 99 Streets in Annual Capital Program

The City of Columbus will repave 99 streets in the second resurfacing project funded by the 2024 capital budget, adding to the 97 streets included in the first 2024 project for a total capital resurfacing investment this year of approximately $30.3 million.

The Resurfacing – 2024 Project 2 will also construct 326 Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) new curb ramps along these 99 streets that are located throughout Columbus. The work will begin next construction season.

“Repaired and repaved pavement on streets in neighborhoods all around our city provides safe, smooth travel for driving, biking or crossing the street,” said Director Kelly Scocco of the Department of Public Service. “The city’s resurfacing program is an important commitment in the city’s capital budget to ensure we properly maintain city streets that serve all residents.”

On Monday, City Council authorized a $13.6 million contract with Strawser Paving Co. to complete the resurfacing project. Construction has progressed on some streets in the first 2024 package, and work will resume on remaining roadways in the spring.

“The investment in improving our local roadways is an investment in our neighborhoods,” said Councilmember Lourdes Barroso de Padilla, chair of the Public Service and Transportation Committee. “The city’s annual street resurfacing program improves safe access to jobs, education, healthcare and other services and amenities for our residents’ quality of life.”

The Department of Public Service manages the city’s resurfacing program, identifying streets throughout Columbus that are most in need of repaving by evaluating maintenance needs and pavement conditions.

Street resurfacing starts with milling, or grinding up, the old asphalt. Where needed, full depth repairs are made before laying new pavement. Concrete work to install the new ADA ramps replaces curb and sidewalk associated with the new ramps. Residents are notified before resurfacing begins on their street.

A map and list of the 99 streets to be resurfaced in Resurfacing –  2024 Project 2 are here.

item.title: City of Columbus Adds Food Waste Drop-Off Sites and Locations for Pumpkin Recycling
item.description:
For Immediate Release

October 30, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467

dsbriner@columbus.gov

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

City of Columbus Opens Four More Food Waste Drop-Off Sites for Residents' Use

Other Refuse Collection Locations will Take Pumpkins, Yard Signs in November for Recycling

The City of Columbus has opened four more community locations where residents can take food scraps for composting, and it is hosting drop-off collection in November for pumpkins and campaign yard signs at its two Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers, including the new Georgesville Road location.

The Division of Refuse Collection services offer residents convenient, sustainable diposal options to divert these materials from the Franklin County landfill. The four new food scraps drop-off sites feature marked collection containers in outdoor enclosures at these Recreation and Parks locations:

  • Beatty Park and Community Center – 247 N. Ohio Ave., 43203
  • Northeast Park and Howard Community Center – 2505 Cassady Ave., 43219
  • Linden Park and Community Center – 1350 Briarwood Ave., 43211
  • Carriage Place Community Center – 4900 Sawmill Rd., 43235

“We are excited to expand accessible drop-off services in more neighborhoods throughout Columbus as residents look for options to sustainably dispose of food waste and divert it from the landfill,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Expansion of residential services marks our commitment to meeting the city’s Climate Action Plan goals to reduce landfill waste and greenhouse gas emissions for a healthy, clean Columbus.”

The new drop-off sites build on the success of three food scraps locations launched in 2023 by Refuse Collection. Since then, residents’ usage at the Bill McDonald Athletic Complex, Dodge Park and Community Center, and Scioto Southland Park has diverted more than 100,000 pounds of food waste from the landfill.

Residents may also bring food scraps to Refuse Collection’s two drive-through Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers, at 2100 Alum Creek Dr., and the newly opened location at 1550 Georgesville Rd.

Visit columbus.gov/foodwaste to learn what food scraps items are accepted for drop-off. The first 300 residents who register on the website may receive a free household bucket to collect and transport their food scraps. Residents may also use their own bucket.

“The Division of Refuse Collection continues to launch innovative services that provide convenience and encourage residents to partner with us in reducing waste taken to the landfill,” said Director Kelly Scocco of the Department of Public Service. “We also offer seasonal collections for residents’ use, such as our drop-off services during November for pumpkin and yard sign recycling.”

In November, the Convenience Centers will accept pumpkins that are free of paint and markers for composting. To reduce contamination, pumpkins should not be dropped off at the city’s food waste sites.

Pumpkins may also be taken in November to the Stephen Lennon Refuse Collection Station, 4260 Morse Road, Monday through Friday, and Saturday, Nov. 2 and Nov. 30,  8 a.m. to noon. These drop-off services diverted more than 13.5 tons from the landfill in 2023.

In addition, the Convenience Centers will accept cardboard, paper, and plastic yard signs and metal wire stands, such as campaign signs, in November. Paper and cardboard signs may be placed in residents’ blue recycling containers, but plastic signs and metal wires should not be.

Visit https://www.columbus.gov/Services/Trash-Recycling-Bulk-Collection to learn more about all items accepted for donation, recycling or disposal at the Convenience Centers, which are open Tuesday through Saturday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

item.title: City of Columbus Bikeways Draft Vision Network Ready for Public Comment
item.description:
For Immediate Release

June 3, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467

dsbriner@columbus.gov

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

City of Columbus Bike Plus Draft Vision Network Ready for Public Feedback

Residents have an opportunity through June to share their comments on an interactive map of the draft vision network developed by the City of Columbus Bike Plus planning initiative. The Bike Plus Plan, led by the Department of Public Service, will improve and expand connections that support safe and comfortable travel in the city by biking, scooting and rolling.

The draft vision network outlines proposed route improvements for safe and equitable city bikeway infrastructure that includes separated bikeways such as shared-use paths and protected on-street lanes, bike lanes or buffered lanes, bike boulevards and trails. A glossary that defines these types of bikeway infrastructure is available on the Bike Plus website here.

“We are eager to hear from the public on the Bike Plus draft vision network—shaped largely by earlier community engagement—to help the city advance a bikeways plan that connects neighborhoods and increases safe access to work, school, entertainment and other amenities and services,” said Public Service Director Kelly Scocco. “Bike Plus will make it more convenient and comfortable to get around Columbus without a car, for equitable and sustainable transportation.”

The Bike Plus planning process launched in 2023. An initial interactive map sought residents’ input to help identify locations where they face challenges and barriers to biking, scooting and rolling, such as safety concerns due to fast-moving vehicle traffic and missing bikeway or trail and path connections.

In addition, the Bike Plus planning team gathered community input through an online survey, pop-up events, a workshop with stakeholders, a series of public office hours, and four open houses this spring where residents could mark up maps to help develop the draft vision network with potential priority projects and policy recommendations.

All of this community engagement helped to shape the draft vision network. Now, residents can provide feedback again on the proposed bikeway projects shown on the draft network’s interactive map.

The final Bike Plus Plan will consider this public feedback and the city’s technical review and feasibility analysis that is currently in progress. Bikeway infrastructure projects will be identified where they are most needed for completion in the short term, and other connections will be completed as the full network is built out over the coming years.

The draft vision network focuses on City of Columbus bikeways infrastructure. Connections with neighboring communities will be coordinated with those jurisdictions.

A finalized Bike Plus Plan will be presented to City Council later this year for proposed adoption.

item.title: Keep Columbus Beautiful Set for KickButt Columbus! Cleanup on March 9
item.description:
For Immediate Release

February 29, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner, Department of Public Service

614-645-6467; dsbriner@columbus.gov

Contact: Aryeh Alex, Keep Columbus Beautiful; 614-338-5004 

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

 

KickButt Columbus! Will Tackle Cigarette Butts and Other Litter on March 9

More than 250 volunteers are signed up for 2024 KickButt Columbus! on Saturday, March 9, to attack cigarette butts, paper, cans, bottles and other trash littering highway ramps in the city.

KickButt Columbus! is the largest annual volunteer cleanup managed by the Keep Columbus Beautiful program in the Department of Public Service. This year’s cleanup will target approximately 40 highway ramps around Columbus.

In 2023, nearly 19,000 pounds—more than 9 tons—of litter was picked up by approximately 220 KickButt Columbus! volunteers during the one-day cleanup. KickButt raises awareness about the environmental harm of littered cigarette butts.

“Thank you to the KickButt Columbus! volunteers who do the hard work each spring of cleaning up highway ramp areas where litter is common,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Let’s respect their efforts, and the health and welfare of our neighborhoods and environment, by choosing not to litter.” 

“KickButt Columbus! volunteers do an incredible job in just one Saturday morning of picking up litter and beautifying highway ramps in our city,” said Kelly Scocco, Public Service Interim Director. “These dedicated residents are working toward solving an issue that harms our community and the environment we all share. Each of us can help end littering by responsibly throwing away our trash in public receptacles or in our containers at home, not on the ground.”

Registration is still open to be a KickButt volunteer. Sign up at keepcolumbusbeautiful@columbus.gov, or call 614-645-2421. Participants will meet at 9 a.m. at the Goodale Park Shelter House, 120 W. Goodale St., Columbus, to get their supplies and then go to designated cleanup locations.

KickButt Columbus! partners include Green Columbus, Friends of the Lower Olentangy Watershed, Friends of the Alum Creek Tributaries, Hashtag59, Clear Creeks and Byways and numerous other community groups, area commissions and nonprofit organizations.

Follow Keep Columbus Beautiful on Facebook and Instagram for information on Kickbutt Columbus!, the upcoming 2024 Columbus Litter League season and other volunteer efforts to fight litter in our community.

City of Columbus to Add Locations, Extend Hours for Short North Rideshare Pickup Zones

The number of designated rideshare pickup zones on High Street in the Short North Arts District, and hours of operation, will expand beginning at midnight on Thursday, Feb. 8, through a partnership among the City of Columbus, Short North Alliance, COTA, Lyft and Uber.

A total of 15 no-parking zones will be designated for rideshare pickup use from midnight to 4 a.m. daily on High St between Goodale Street and 5th Avenue. Nine of the rideshare zones will be located at COTA stops in this section of  High Street since bus service ends by midnight.

The city launched a successful pilot program in summer 2022 with eight designated pickup zones to create a safe environment for managing rideshare activity, parking and traffic flow along areas of High Street with the most late-night activity in the popular Short North Arts District. The new hours extend the pickup end time from 3 a.m. to 4 a.m.

The rideshare zones provide convenient, predictable pickup access for customers and drivers, encourage responsible rideshare use and discourage impaired driving. They help to minimize double parking, traffic congestion and sidewalk overcrowding.

Those who are using rideshare services when visiting the Short North Arts District will be directed by the service’s app to the nearest pickup zone. The rideshare driver will be notified a customer is waiting in that zone for a ride.

item.title: City of Columbus to Resurface 79 More Neighborhood Streets
item.description:
For Immediate Release

January 10, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467

dsbriner@columbus.gov

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

 

City of Columbus Invests $12.35 Million to Resurface 79 More Neighborhood Streets

A third street resurfacing project in the City of Columbus 2023 capital improvements budget will repave 79 streets and construct 340 ADA-compliant curb ramps at intersections along the streets in an investment of $12.35 million.

The third package of streets in the city’s 2023 resurfacing program brings the total to 209 neighborhood streets being repaved throughout Columbus and 870 Americans with Disabilities curb ramps being constructed, marking a capital investment of nearly $35.2 million.

“The  resurfacing program is a critical part of the city’s annual capital  budget that supports all neighborhoods and extends the life of our city roadways,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Newly paved and repaired steets with upgraded curb ramps make travel safe and smooth for residents, whether they are driving, walking or biking.”

On Monday, City Council authorized a $12.35 million contract with Strawser Paving Co. to complete the third 2023 resurfacing package, beginning in the upcoming construction season. Resurfacing of the 59 streets in the first project of 2023 has been completed, and work will resume on the second package of 71 streets this spring.

The Department of Public Service manages the city’s street resurfacing program, to evaluate maintenance needs and pavement conditions of all Columbus roadways totaling more than 5,600 lane miles.

Street resurfacing is a multistep process that includes milling the old pavement, making deep pavement repairs where needed, and laying new pavement, first a tack coat to help asphalt adhere to the roadway and then the final asphalt layer. Concrete work to install new ADA curb ramps begins the process. Residents are notified before resurfacing of their street is set to begin.

A map and list of the 79 streets to be resurfaced in Resurfacing –  2023 Project 3 is here.

item.title: Columbus Waste & Reuse Convenience Center Helps Residents with Post-Holiday Cleanup
item.description:
For Immediate Release

December 22, 2023

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467 (office); 614-619-0917 (cell); dsbriner@columbus.gov

Contact: Aryeh Alex - Keep Columbus Beautiful, Division of Refuse Collection 614-338-5004 (cell)

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

City of Columbus Waste and Reuse Convenience Center Helps Residents Sustainably Dispose of, Reuse or Recycle a Variety of Items

The New Service Offers a One-Stop Solution for Cleanup After the Holidays

The holidays can generate more household trash, and often you aren’t sure how to dispose of it the right way. What can you do with your Christmas tree or the string lights that have finally flickered out? The leftover food you can’t eat anymore? If Santa gave you a new computer or phone, how do you dispose of the old? Is your blue recycling container so full you can’t stuff one more shipping box or ball of crumpled gift wrap in it?

The City of Columbus offers an environmentally-friendly, one-stop solution at no cost to residents: the new Refuse Collection Waste and Reuse Convenience Center at 2100 Alum Creek Dr., Columbus 43207. 

The Convenience Center, open since November, provides Columbus residents with drive-through service to sustainably dispose of, recycle or reuse a variety of items — from food scraps for composting, to furniture and clothing in good condition for reuse, to electronics and many other materials for recycling.

In addition, the Convenience Center accepts some seasonal items. Right now, that means string lights and real Christmas trees (with lights, decorations and tinsel removed). Trees may also be set out with your yard waste for regular collection though January. Trees taller than 8 feet should be cut in sections.

See a full list of items that can, and cannot, be dropped off at the Convenience Center here. 

Hours of operation are Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Refuse Collection staff are there to help residents with proper sorting of items. Please note: The Convenience Center will be closed on Tuesday, Dec. 26, and Tuesday, Jan. 2.

The Convenience Center supplements Refuse Collection’s other residential services, including weekly trash and recycling and biweekly yard waste collection and scheduled bulk pickup.

Residents are increasingly interested in practicing reduce, reuse and recycle to decrease the amount of household trash being landfilled. The city’s expanding services offer convenient options to support this and to help achieve Columbus Climate Action Plan goals.

For the first time last year, Refuse Collection hosted a post-Christmas, drive-through recycling event encouraging residents to drop off old electronics and extra cardboard and gift wrap instead of tossing them in the trash. Hundreds of vehicles drove through, and more than 15 tons of materials were collected and diverted from the landfill during the one-day event.

The collection helped to shape the planning and opening of the Waste and Reuse Convenience Center. A second center is set to open at Refuse Collection’s Georgesville Road refuse transfer station in early 2024.

614-645-6467

dsbriner@columbus.gov

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

City of Columbus New PickUp CBUS App Offers Easy Access to Residential Trash and Recycling Collection Information

The Columbus Division of Refuse Collection has launched the PickUp CBUS app to provide another convenient service for residents to get their trash and recycling pickup schedules, sign up for reminders and service updates and check on whether items are recyclable.

The free PickUp CBUS app for smartphone use is available to download on the App Store and Google Play.

“The Department of Public Service and our Division of Refuse Collection focus on delivering quality services and tools like the new PickUp CBUS app that support convenience for residents and their desire to practice sustainability through recycling and reuse options,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “With our residential services, we can achieve the city’s Climate Action Plan waste diversion goals to create a healthier community for everyone.”

The Waste Wizard feature on the PickUp CBUS app allows residents to search an item to learn if it can be placed in their blue recycling collection cart, or can be recycled or reused  through other area drop-off services, including those offered by the city.

“By continuing to expand core services focused on reduce, reuse and recycling, Refuse Collection is leading the way to assist residents in diverting recoverable materials from the landfill, supporting a circular economy and improving the quality of the environment,” Public Service Director Jennifer L. Gallagher said.

Residents should watch their mailboxes early next year for a postcard that has more information about what is and isn't recyclable in your blue container, and a scannable code to directly download the PickUp CBUS app. The city is providing this resource thanks to a grant from The Recycling Partnership, with support from the American Beverage’s Every Bottle Back initiative and the Ohio Beverage Association.

The PickUp CBUS app is the latest in a series of Refuse Collection service enhancements added this year for more convenience and recycling and disposal options that support sustainability. Residential recycling collection expanded to weekly service, and the city opened three neighborhood drop-off locations to collect food waste for composting.

Refuse Collection also recently opened its first Waste and Reuse Convenience Center at 2100 Alum Creek Dr., where Columbus residents at no cost may bring acceptable items for sustainable disposal, reuse or recycling.

The Convenience Center is open Tuesday through Saturday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with Refuse Collection staff there to assist residents with correct sorting of items they bring. The city intends to open a second Convenience Center on Georgesville Road early next year.

In addition to using the PickUp CBUS app, residents may visit the Refuse Collection page on the City of Columbus website here to learn more about residential trash, recycling and yard waste collection and new drop-off services, including items that are acceptable to drop off at the Convenience Center.

Drop-Off Options: For recycling drop-off locations see https://recycleright.org/recycling locations/?category=49; for yard waste drop-off locations see https://new.columbus.gov/Services/Trash-Recycling-Bulk-Collection/Yard-Waste-Collection or contact the 311 Service Center online at https://www.columbus.gov/311/, by email at 311@columbus.gov or at (614) 645-3111.

Residents may check their collection days and set collection schedule reminders on our website at: www.columbus.gov/publicservice/Refuse-Collection/.

Parking Kiosks and Meters: Motorists may park free of charge at kiosks and meters on Thursday, Nov. 23. Parking restriction signage at some kiosks and meters will be enforced, including but not limited to morning and evening rush hours and zones marked for valets, taxis, loading, handicapped-only and residential permit parking areas.

Offices Closed: Department offices, including the Parking Violations Bureau and the Right-of-Way Permits Office, will be closed on Thursday, Nov. 23.  Permits may be filed online at https://ca.columbus.gov/ca/.

item.title: City of Columbus Sets Drop-Off Sites for Sustainable Disposal of Pumpkins, Yard Signs
item.description:
For Immediate Release

October 30, 2023

Contact: Debbie Briner, Department of Public Service

614-645-6467; dsbriner@columbus.gov

Contact: Aryeh Alex, Keep Columbus Beautiful

614-338-5004; awalex@columbus.gov

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

City of Columbus to Host Environmentally-Friendly Drop-Off Collection of Residents’ Pumpkins and Yard Signs

The City of Columbus Division of Refuse Collection will host drop-off sites after Halloween and Election Day for residents to sustainably dispose of pumpkins, gourds and yard signs. The drive-through service will prevent these items from being landfilled or contaminating yard waste and the residential blue recycling containers serviced by the city’s collection program.

Carved jack-o-lantern with candles removed, full and moldy pumpkins and gourds are acceptable to drop off for composting at the drive-through sites. Pumpkins decorated with paint or permanent marker cannot be accepted.

The pumpkin drop-off collection sites will operate on three Saturdays — Nov. 4, Nov. 25 and Dec. 2 — from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Columbus Refuse Collection transfer stations:

  • 2100 Alum Creek Dr., 43207
  • 1550 Georgesville Rd., 43228
  • 4260 Morse Rd., 43230

To reduce contamination, pumpkins may not be dropped off at the city’s three food scraps drop-off sites. For more information on how to use the food scraps sites visit https://www.columbus.gov/foodwaste/.

The drive-through yard sign recycling event will be held on Nov. 11, the Saturday after Election Day, from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Alum Creek Refuse Collection station, 2100 Alum Creek Dr.

Residents also have the option to take their signs to SWACO's sign recycling event location at the Bill McDonald Athletic Complex, 4990 Olentangy River Rd, from 8 a.m. to noon on Nov. 11.

All paper, plastic and coroplast signs (including metal stands) will be accepted and recycled free of charge thanks to a partnership with SWACO, the Solid Waste Authority of Central Ohio.

Plastic and coroplast signs, and their metal stands should not be put in the residential blue recycling containers due to the materials used to make them. However, it is acceptable to put paper yard signs (without metal stands) in the blue cart.
